manuscript: RA-SCOPE: Support-Backed Full-Consensus Projection for Ordinal Picturebook Grading
claim_policy: Every quantitative claim must be reproducible from a named artifact; formal claims must map to executable code and tests; limitations define the supported scope.

claims.claim: Projection activates only when all anchors agree and at least one anchor is support-qualified; a singleton supported anchor cannot create consensus.
claims.validation: Executable unit tests cover agreeing supported anchors, disagreeing anchors with one supported anchor, and agreement without support.

claims.claim: The retained-margin operator is the unique Euclidean projection onto the active feasible set, yields a monotone cumulative distribution, and preserves the activated consensus grade.
claims.validation: Closed-form implementation, mathematical proof, invariant tests, and empirical preservation counts agree.

claims.claim: On 120 adjudicated books, RA-SCOPE obtains QWK 0.822717, MAE 0.416667, exact accuracy 0.591667, within-one accuracy 0.991667, and error-above-one rate 0.008333.
Independent P01--P03 ratings yield ordinal Krippendorff alpha 0.677 [0.594, 0.740] for 120 global grades and 0.586 [0.524, 0.638] for 1,200 criterion units.
claims.unit: book-bootstrap for global grades and criterion-unit summary

claims.claim: Main-set QWK differences versus uniform pooling, length, MacBERT, and Qwen2.5-3B are +0.032, +0.056, +0.060, and +0.285; their 95% paired lineage-bootstrap intervals exclude zero.
claims.resampling: 10,000 paired percentile-bootstrap samples over original-work lineages

claims.claim: On the separately adjudicated 28-book collection, RA-SCOPE obtains QWK 0.786111, MAE 0.392857, exact accuracy 0.607143, and no errors above one level.
claims.boundary: The sample is small and contains no L5 or L6 books.

claims.claim: The main collection has 38 activated consensuses, 46 supported conflicts, and 36 no-support cases; activated grades are preserved in 38/38 main, 32/32 source-OOF, and 7/7 robustness cases.
Across tested support cutoffs, main QWK ranges from 0.817 to 0.825 and robustness QWK remains 0.786; tested retained margins do not change point predictions.
claims.boundary: This is a finite grid sensitivity analysis, not a universal invariance claim.

claims.claim: Experts disagree on 104/120 main books, mean pairwise disagreement is 0.576389, 42 prediction patterns occur, and every expert is uniquely exact on at least four books.
Relative to uniform pooling, RA-SCOPE improves ordinal Brier score, class NLL, and MAE risk-coverage AUC, while ECE increases slightly.
claims.boundary: Probability metrics are descriptive on the 120-book main collection.

claims.claim: After controlling log characters, log pages, and source, RA-SCOPE partial Spearman correlation is 0.400 with 95% interval [0.258, 0.545], while the length expert is -0.034 [-0.091, 0.090]; RA-SCOPE orders 17/24 counter-length pairs correctly.
StoryWeaver and Global ASP slices obtain QWK/MAE 0.775/0.416 and 0.795/0.391; band-wise MAE is 0.500, 0.375, and 0.353 for L1--L2, L3, and L4--L5.
claims.boundary: The eight-book GDL slice is descriptive only.

claims.claim: The mean of ten criterion grades correlates 0.935 [0.907, 0.952] with global grade and retains partial Spearman 0.720 [0.589, 0.800] after length, pages, and source controls.
claims.boundary: This is internal convergent evidence from common professional annotators, not learner-comprehension validity.

claims.claim: Observable-modality specialists increase criterion macro-QWK from 0.456 to 0.532 and reduce macro-MAE by 0.119; the illustration and pinyin specialists improve their designated criteria.
claims.boundary: Specialist routing is supporting criterion evidence; it is not part of the global RA-SCOPE projection.

claims.claim: The deterministic Qwen2.5-3B rubric baseline uses restricted next-token scoring and obtains QWK/MAE 0.538/0.825 on main and 0.603/0.714 on robustness.
claims.boundary: This baseline characterizes one open 3B zero-shot configuration and does not generalize to all LLMs.

claims.claim: Evidence is strongest for L1--L4; L5 is descriptive and L6 is untested; learner comprehension and prospective upper-level validation remain outside the present evidence.
